nodes.statement: We only provide a sketch of the full proof (SM ). The main idea is to divide [0,T] into M uniform subintervals and construct a neural network that approximates a Taylor approximation in time of u in each subinterval. In the obtained formula, we approximate the monomials and multiplications by neural networks (SM ) and approximate the derivatives of u by finite differences and use of SM to find an error estimate in C^k([0,T], L^q(D))-norm. We use again finite difference operators to prove that spatial derivatives of u are accurately approximated as well. The neural network will also approximately satisfy the initial/boundary conditions as Vert u_theta-uVert_L^2(partial([0,T]times D)) lesssim C poly(d) Vert u_theta-uVert_H^1([0,T]times D), which follows from a Sobolev trace inequality.
nodes.raw_latex: We only provide a sketch of the full proof (\textbf{SM} \ref{app:nn-to-pinn}). The main idea is to divide $[0,T]$ into $M$ uniform subintervals and construct a neural network that approximates a Taylor approximation in time of $u$ in each subinterval. In the obtained formula, we approximate the monomials and multiplications by neural networks (\textbf{SM} \ref{app:nnt}) and approximate the derivatives of $u$ by finite differences and use \eqref{eq:accuracy-FD} of \textbf{SM} \ref{app:FD} to find an error estimate in $C^k([0,T], L^q(D))$-norm. We use again finite difference operators to prove that spatial derivatives of $u$ are accurately approximated as well. The neural network will also approximately satisfy the initial/boundary conditions as $\Vert u_\theta-u\Vert_{L^2(\partial([0,T]\times D))} \lesssim C \mathrm{poly}(d) \Vert u_\theta-u\Vert_{H^1([0,T]\times D)}$, which follows from a Sobolev trace inequality.

nodes.statement: We follow the proof of . All steps of the proofs are identical, with the only difference being that the W^k,infty([0,1]^d)-norm of is replaced by the C^k([0,T], L^2(mu))-norm in this work. Following , one divides the domain [0,T] into intervals I_i^N = [t_i-1, t_i], with t_i=iT/N and NinN large enough. On each of these intervals, f locally can be approximated (in Sobolev norm) by p_j^N, by virtue of the assumptions of the theorem. A global approximation can then be constructed by multiplying each p_j^N with an approximation of the indicator function of the corresponding intervals and summing over all intervals. We now highlight the main steps in the proof. Step 2a (as in ) results in the following estimate, hkif-sum_j=1^N f cdot Phi^N_j leq C hkif left(varepsilon +N^k+1 ln^kleft(fracCN^kvarepsilonright)varepsilonright). Step 2b results in the estimate, hkisum_j=1^N (f -p_j^N)cdot Phi^N,d_jleq C ln^kleft(fracCN^kvarepsilonright)left[fracC_kN^s-k + xi N^k + C_k N^k+1 varepsilonright], Putting everything together, we find that if CN^kgeq varepsilone, &hkunitf-sum_j=1^N p_j^Ncdot Phi^N_j \\& leq C ln^kleft(fracCN^kvarepsilonright)left[(hkif+C_k)N^k+1varepsilon+ fracC_kN^s-k + xi N^kright]. In particular, if we set N^k+1varepsilon = N^-s+k and Ngeq 3, then we find that hkunitf-sum_j=1^N p_j^Ncdot Phi^N_j leq C ln^kleft(Nright)left[frachkif+C_kN^s-k + xi N^kright].

nodes.statement: Step 1: construction. To define the approximation, we divide [0,T] into M subintervals of the form [t_m-1,t_m], where t_m = mT/M with 1leq mleq M. One could approximate u on every subinterval by an s-th order accurate Taylor approximation around t_m, provided that one has access to D^i_t u(cdot, t_m) for 0leq i leq s-1. As those values are unknown, we resort to the finite difference approximation D^i_t u(cdot, t_m)approx M^icdot Delta^i,s-i_1/M,t[U^varepsilon(u_0,t_m)], which is a neural network. See SM for an overview of the notation for finite difference operators. Moreover, we replace the univariate monomials varphi_i:[0,T]toR: tmapsto t^i in the Taylor approximation by neural networks widehatvarphi_i^delta:[0,T]toR with Vertvarphi_i-widehatvarphi_i^deltaVert_C^k+1lesssim delta. Lemma guarantees that the output of (widehatvarphi_i^delta)_i=1^s-1 can be obtained using a shallow network with width 2(s+1) (independent of delta). The multiplication operator is replaced by a shallow neural network widehattimes_delta: [-a,a]^2toR (for suitable a>0) for which Verttimes-widehattimes_deltaVert_C^k+1lesssim delta. By Lemma only four neurons are needed for this network. This results in the following approximation for fin C^0([0,T]times D), widehatN^delta_m[f](t,x) := sum_i=0^s-1 widehattimes_deltaleft(fracDelta^i,s-i_1/M,t[f](t_m,x)M^-i i!, widehatvarphi_i^delta(t-t_m)right) forall tin [0,T], \: xin D, \: 1leq mleq M. Next, we patch together these individual approximations by (approximately) multiplying them with a NN approximation of a partition of unity, denoted by Phi^M_1, ldots, Phi^M_M:[0,T]to[0,1], as introduced in Definition in SM . Every Phi_m^M can be thought of as a NN approximation of the indicator function on [t_m-1,t_m]. For any varepsilon,delta>0, we then define our final neural network approximation widehatu:[0,T]times Dto R as, widehatu(t,x) := sum_m=1^M widehattimes_delta left(widehatN^delta_m[U^varepsilon(u_0,t_m)](t,x), Phi^M_m(t)right) forall tin [0,T], \: xin D. Step 2: error estimate. In order to facilitate the proof, we introduce the intermediate approximations Tildeu:[0,T]times Dto R and N_m:C^0(D)times [0,T]times Dto R by, Tildeu(t,x) := sum_m=1^M N_m[widehatu^varepsilon_m](t,x)cdot Phi^M_m(t) := sum_m=1^M sum_i=0^s-1 fracDelta^i,s-i_1/M,t[widehatu^varepsilon_m](t_m,x)M^-i i!cdot varphi_i(t-t_m)cdot Phi^M_m(t), where widehatu^varepsilon_m = U^varepsilon(u_0,t_m). Note that widehatu can be obtained from Tildeu by replacing the multiplication operator and the monomials by neural networks. Since these the size of these networks are independent of their accuracy delta, we can assume without loss of generality that Vert D^(k,bmalpha)(Tildeu-widehatu)(t,cdot)Vert_L^qleq delta (see Lemma ) for any relevant D^(k,bmalpha) and t. It remains to prove that D^(k,bmalpha)Tildeu approx D^(k,bmalpha)u. Combining the observation that D^(k,bmalpha)N_m[widehatu^varepsilon_m] = D_t^k N_m[D^bmalpha_xwidehatu^varepsilon_m] with Lemma lets us conclude that for all 0leq kleq s-1 and tin[t_m-2, t_m+2], normD^(k,bmalpha)( N_m[widehatu^varepsilon_m](t,cdot)-u(t,cdot))_L^q leq C(r)M^k(normD^bmalpha_x(widehatu^varepsilon_m-u)(cdot,t_m)_L^q+absu_C^(s,ell)M^-s) We use Theorem with fleftarrow u, p_j^N leftarrow N_m[D^bmalpha_xwidehatu^varepsilon_m], xileftarrow C(r)M^k normD^bmalpha_x(widehatu^varepsilon_m-u)(cdot,t_m)_L^q, C^*_ell leftarrow C(s)absu_C^(k,ell), Nleftarrow M to find that, normD^(k,bmalpha)(widehatu-u)_L^q leq Cln^k(M)(normu_C^(s,ell)M^k-s+M^2knormD^bmalpha_x(widehatu^varepsilon_m-u)(cdot,t_m)_L^q), where C(r,s)>0 only depend on r and s. Finally, using Lemma to bound normD^bmalpha_x(widehatu^varepsilon_m-u)(cdot,t_m)_L^q and combining this with Assumption proves . Step 3: size estimate. The following holds, depth(widehatu)leq Cdepth(U^varepsilon), width(widehatu) leq CM width(U^varepsilon).

nodes.statement: Step 1: construction. Let NinN, let E_N: C^0(T^d)to R^absJ_N be an encoder and Q_N: R^absJ_Nto L^2_N be a trigonometric polynomial interpolation operator, cf. SM . If we let widehatG = U^varepsilon circ Q_N circ E_N then we can define an FNO G_theta: L^2_N(T^d)to L^2_N(T^d) as G_theta(u_0)(x) = (Q_Ncirc E_N circ widehatG)(u_0)(x). Step 2: error estimate. We decompose the L^2-error of the FNO using the triangle inequality and the inequality VertU^varepsilon-widehatGVert_L^2leq C^varepsilon_stabnormu_0-Q_NcircE_Ncirc u_0_L^p, which follows from Assumption , normG-G_theta_L^2 &leq normG-U^varepsilon_L^2 + C^varepsilon_stabnormu_0-Q_NcircE_Ncirc u_0_L^p+ VertwidehatG-G_thetaVert_L^2. First, we find using a Sobolev embedding result (Lemma ) and Lemma that, normu_0-(Q_NcircE_N)(u_0)_L^pleq normu_0-(Q_NcircE_N)(u_0)_H^d/p^* leq C(d,r) N^-r+d/p^*normu_0_H^r, where p^* is such that 1/p+1/p^*=1/2. Next, we observe that for any u_0inX with normu_0_C^rleq B that norm(Q_NcircE_N)(u_0)_H^r(T^d) leq C B=:BarB. Hence, by applying Lemma to the second and last term of we find that, normG-G_theta_L^2 leq C(varepsilon + C^varepsilon_stabBN^-r+d/p^*+ C_varepsilon,r^BarBN^-r). Step 3: size estimate. As for any FNO, the width is equal to N^dwidth(U^varepsilon). The depth in this case is equal to depth(U^varepsilon).

We decompose the L^2-error of the FNO using the triangle inequality and the inequality VertU^varepsilon-widehatGVert_L^2leq C^varepsilon_stabnormu_0-Q_NcircE_Ncirc u_0_L^p, which follows from Assumption , normG-G_theta_L^2 &leq normG-U^varepsilon_L^2 + C^varepsilon_stabnormu_0-Q_NcircE_Ncirc u_0_L^p+ VertwidehatG-G_thetaVert_L^2. First, we find using a Sobolev embedding result (Lemma ) and Lemma that, normu_0-(Q_NcircE_N)(u_0)_L^pleq normu_0-(Q_NcircE_N)(u_0)_H^d/p^* leq C(d,r) N^-r+d/p^*normu_0_H^r, where p^* is such that 1/p+1/p^*=1/2. Next, we observe that for any u_0inX with normu_0_C^rleq B that norm(Q_NcircE_N)(u_0)_H^r(T^d) leq C B=:BarB. Hence, by applying Lemma to the second and last term of we find that, normG-G_theta_L^2 leq C(varepsilon + C^varepsilon_stabBN^-r+d/p^*+ C_varepsilon,r^BarBN^-r). Step 3: size estimate. As for any FNO, the width is equal to N^dwidth(U^varepsilon). The depth in this case is equal to depth(U^varepsilon).

Lemma . Using notation from SM , let Q_N:R^absJ_Nto C(T^d) be the trigonometric polynomial interpolation operator as in and let E_N:C(T^d)toR^absJ_N be the encoder as in . We define widehatQ_N:R^absJ_Nto C(T^d): y mapsto frac1absK_N sum_kin K_N sum_jin J_N y_j a_k,j widehatbme_k, with coefficients a_k,j as in , as a neural network approximation of Q_N. Inspired by the proof of Theorem (and using its notation as well), we define widehatG: C(T^d)to L^2(mu) by widehatG(u_0)(t,x) = sum_m=1^Msum_i=0^s-1 fracDelta^i,s-i_1/M[U^varepsilon(Q_ZcircE_Zcirc u_0, t_m)](t_m,x)M^-i i!cdot varphi_i^delta(t-t_m) Phi^M_m(t), Then it holds that (Q_NcircE_NcircwidehatG)(u_0)(t,x) &= sum_kin K_N sum_jin J_N sum_m=1^Msum_i=0^s-1 fraca_k,jabsK_N fracDelta^i,s-i_1/M[U^varepsilon(Q_ZcircE_Zcirc u_0, t_m)](t_m,x_j)M^-i i!cdot Psi_i,m,k(t,x)\\ Psi_i,m,k(t,x) &= varphi_i^delta(t-t_m) Phi^M_m(t) bme_k(x). Now for every i, m, k let Psi_i,m,k:[0,T]times T^dto R be defined as, widehatPsi_i,m,k(t,x) = widehattimes_deltaleft(varphi_i^delta(t-t_m),Phi^M_m(t),widehatbme _k(x)right), where widehattimes_delta is a neural network approximation of the multiplication operator. Next, we observe that using Assumption , Assumption and it holds that for all t, norm(U^varepsilon(Q_Zcirc E_Zcirc u_0)-G(u_0))(cdot,t)_L^2 leq varepsilon + C^varepsilon_stabCBZ^-r+d/p^*. Finally, using Lemma we find that normD^(k,bmalpha)(widehatQ_Ncirc E_Ncirc widehatG-G_theta)(u_0)_L^2leq delta. By setting eta = N^ell-r-d, h=1/N and using that M^2kleq M^k+s-1 and C_varepsilon,ell^BarBleq C_varepsilon,r^BarB we find, normL(G-G_theta)_L^2 leq Cln^k(M)(normu_C^(s,ell)M^k-s+M^k+s-1((varepsilon+C^varepsilon_stabZ^-r+d/p^*)N^ell+C^BarB_varepsilon,rN^ell-r)). We conclude by using that ln^k(M)leq CM^rho for any rho>0. Step 3: size estimate. nodes.statement: Step 1: construction of the neural network. Let varepsilon,delta>0 be arbitrary and let widehatF = widehatF_delta, widehatg=widehatg_delta and I=I_delta as in Setting . We then define for all ninN and thetainTheta, widehatU_n^theta(t,x) & = frac\1_N(n)m^n br[Bigg] sum_k=1^m^n (I^n-1circwidehatg)pr[bigl]x + W_T-t^(theta,0,-k) \\ & + sum_i=0^n-1 frac(T-t)m^n-ibr[Bigg] sum_k=1^m^n-i pr[] (I^n-i-1circwidehatF)(widehatU_i^(theta,i,k)) - \1_N(i) (I^n-icircwidehatF)( widehatU_i-1^(theta,-i,k)) pr[] EuScriptU_t^(theta,i,k), x + W_EuScriptU_t^(theta,i,k)-t^(theta,i,k) , with notation and random variables cf. Definition . Note that for every tin[0,T], ninN, thetainTheta, every realization of the random variable widehatU_n^theta(t,cdot) is a neural network that maps from T^d to R. Let ninN_0, minN and tin [0,T] be arbitrary. Integrating the square of the error bound of Theorem and Fubini's theorem tell us that Eint_T^dabsU^0_n(t,x)-u(t,x)^2dmu(x) &= int_T^d EabsU^0_n(t,x)-u(t,x)^2 dmu(x)\\ &leq frac4L^2 (T+1)^2exp(2LT)(1+2LT)^2nm^nexp(-m). From Lemma it then follows that Probint_T^dabsU^0_n(t,x)-u(t,x)^2dmu(x) leq frac4L^2 (T+1)^2exp(2LT)(1+2LT)^2nm^nexp(-m) > 0. As a result, there exists overlineomega=overlineomega(t,n,m)in Omega and a realization U^0_n(overlineomega) such that normU^0_n(overlineomega)(t,cdot)-u(t,cdot)_L^2(mu) leq fracL (T+1)exp(LT)(1+2LT)^nm^n/2exp(-m/2). We define omega : [0,T]times N^2to Omega: (t,n,m)mapsto overlineomega(t,n,m) and set for every 1leq kleq n, widehatU_k,omega^theta(t,x) = widehatU_k^theta(omega(t,n,m))(t,x) and U_k,omega^theta(t,x) = U_k^theta(omega(t,n,m))(t,x) for all kinN_0 and all thetainTheta. We then define our approximation as widehatU_n,omega^0(t,cdot). Step 2: error estimate. We will quantify how well widehatU_n,omega^0 approximates U_n,omega^0. Using the calculation that for f_1,f_2in C^1(R) and h_1, h_2in L^2(mu) it holds that normf_1circ h_1 - f_2circ h_2_L^2(mu) &leq normf_1circ h_1 - f_2circ h_1_L^2(mu) + normf_2circ h_1 - f_2circ h_2_L^2(mu)\\ &leq normf_1-f_2_C^0(R) + absf_2_Lip(R)normh_1-h_2_L^2(mu), and the fact that 2nleq 2^n for ninN we find that it holds for every thetainTheta that, &normwidehatU_n,omega^theta(t,cdot)-U^theta_n,omega(t,cdot)_L^2(mu) \\ & leq \1_N(n) left(normwidehatg-g_L^2(mu)+(n-1)normI-Id_C^0right) + T sum_i=0^n-1 normI^n-i-1circwidehatFcirc widehatU_i,omega^(theta,i,k)-Fcirc U_i,omega^(theta,i,k)_L^2(mu) \\& + T sum_i=0^n-1\1_N(i) normI^n-icircwidehatFcirc widehatU_i-1,omega^(theta,-i,k)-Fcirc U_i-1,omega^(theta,-i,k)_L^2(mu) \\ & leq \1_N(n) left[normwidehatg-g_L^2(mu) + 2TnnormwidehatF-F_C^0(R)+ left((n-1)+frac(n-1)n2+frac(n+1)n2right)normI-Id_C^0right]\\ & + LT sum_i=0^n-1left(normwidehatU_i^(theta,i,k)- U_i^(theta,i,k)_L^2(mu) + \1_N(i)norm widehatU_i-1^(theta,-i,k)- U_i-1^(theta,-i,k)_L^2(mu) right)\\ & leq \1_N(n)2^n left[normwidehatg-g_L^2(mu) + TnormwidehatF-F_C^0(R)+ nnormI-Id_C^0right]\\ & + sum_i=0^n-1 (max\1,LT\)^n-i left(normwidehatU_i^(theta,i,k)- U_i^(theta,i,k)_L^2(mu) + \1_N(i)norm widehatU_i-1^(theta,-i,k)- U_i-1^(theta,-i,k)_L^2(mu) right). , Now let us set for every kinN_0, x_k = sup_thetainTheta normwidehatU_k,omega^theta(t,cdot)-U^theta_k,omega(t,cdot)_L^2(mu), and in addition we define alpha_0 = normwidehatg-g_L^2(mu) +TnormwidehatF-F_C^0(R), alpha_1 = normI-Id_C^0 and beta = 2+LT. Next we define C_1 = (T+1)(1+L exp(LT)), C_2 = 5+3LT. nodes.statement: We prove the claim by induction on ell. Base case. From Definition , we find that for ell = 0 and all kinN_0 it holds that sup_thetainTheta normwidehatU^theta_k,omega_C^0([0,T]timesT^d) leq normwidehatg_C^0(T^d) + 2TnormwidehatF_C^0(R)k. Claim follows immediately for ell=0. Induction step. We assume that claim holds true for all 0leq ell^*leq ell-1 and kinN_0. From this assumption, we will deduce that holds true for ell and all kinN_0. We first observe that it follows from Lemma , the induction hypothesis and the fact that (C_k,ell)_ellgeq0 is non-decreasing for any k, that for all thetainTheta and 0leq i,jleq k it holds that, abs (I^jcircwidehatF)(widehatU^theta_i,omega)_C^ell([0,T]timesT^d) leq normI^jcircwidehatF_C^ell(R)left(B_ell C_k,ell-1^ell+ abs widehatU^theta_i,omega_C^(0,ell)([0,T]timesT^d)right), and where (again using Lemma ) it holds that normI^jcircwidehatF_C^ell(R) leq 2B_ell normwidehatF_C^ell^ell. nodes.statement: We note that each element in the (real) trigonometric basis bme_1,dots, bme_p can be expressed in the form bme_j(x) = cos(kappacdot x), or bme_j(x) = sin(kappacdot x), for kappa = kappa(j)in Z^d with |kappa|_infty le N, where N is chosen as the smallest natural number such that p le (2N+1)^d. We focus only focus on the first form, as the proof for the second form is entirely similar. Define f:[0,2pi]^dtoR:xmapsto kappacdot x and g:[-2pi dN, 2pi dN]toR:xmapsto cos(x). As f([0,2pi]^d) subset [-2pi dN, 2pi dN], the composition gcirc f is well-defined and one can see that it coincides with a trigonometric basis function bme_j. Moreover, the linear map f is a trivial neural network without hidden layers. Approximating bme_j by a neural network tau_j therefore boils down to approximating g by a suitable neural network. From it follows that the function g there exists an independent constant R>0 such that for large enough tinN there is a tanh neural network widehatg_t with two hidden layers and O(t+N) neurons such that normg-widehatg_t_C^s([-2pi dN, 2pi dN]) leq 4 (8(s+1)^3R)^s exp(t-s). This can be proven from by setting deltaleftarrowfrac13, kleftarrow s, sleftarrow t, Nleftarrow 2 and using normg_C^s=1 and Stirling's approximation to obtain frac1(t-s)!left(frac32cdot 2right)^t-s leq frac1sqrt2pi(t-s) left(fracet-sright)^t-s leq exp(s-t) for t>s+e^2. Setting t = O(ln(delta^-1)+sln(s)) then gives a neural network widehatg_t with normg-widehatg_t_C^s<eta. Let $j\in{1,\ldots,p}$. It holds by definition of Legendre polynomials and the corresponding enumeration (\textbf{SM} \ref{app:Legendre}) that the degree in every variable is at most $p$. Therefore, $L_j$ is a product of $d$ univariate polynomials of degree at most $p$. 
From \cite[Lemma 3.2]{deryck2021approximation} it follows that one needs a shallow tanh neural network with $O(p)$ neurons to approximate a univariate polynomial to any accuracy. The result from \cite[Corollary 3.7]{deryck2021approximation} can be used to construct a shallow tanh network that approximates the product of the $d$ univariate polynomials. Note that its size only depends on the dimension $d$ and not on the polynomial degree $p$ or the accuracy. 
Finally, \cite[Lemma A.7]{deryck2021approximation} ensures the accuracy of the composition of the two subnetworks. It then follows that there exist a tanh neural network of width $\mathcal{O}(p)$ and two hidden layers that achieves the wanted error estimate.

\label{thm:holomorphic-approx}
Let $\mathcal{F}: [-1,1]^\mathcal{J} \to L^2(U)$ be $(\bm{b},\varepsilon,\kappa)$-holomorphic with $\bm{b}\in \ell^q(\mathbb{N})$ and $\kappa: \mathbb{N} \to \mathcal{J}$ an enumeration, and assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is given by \eqref{eq:G-parametrized}. Assume that the encoder/decoder pair is constructed as in \cite[Section 3.5.3]{LMK1}, so that \cite[Eq. (3.69)]{LMK1} holds. Given an affine reconstruction $\mathcal{R}: \mathbb{R}^p\to L^2(U)$, let $\mathcal{P}: L^2(U) \to \mathbb{R}^p$ denote the corresponding optimal linear projection \cite[Eq. (3.17)]{LMK1}. Then given $k\in\mathbb{N}$, there exists a constant $C_k>0$, independent of $m$, $p$ and an approximator $\mathcal{A}: \mathbb{R}^m \to \mathbb{R}^p$ that can be represented by a neural network with
\[
\begin{gathered}
\mathrm{size}(\mathcal{A}) 
\le
C_k(1+pm \log(m) ), 
\quad
\mathrm{depth}(\mathcal{A}) \le C_k(1+\log(m)).
\end{gathered}
\]
and such that the approximation error $\widehat{\mathscr{E}}_{\mathcal{A}}$ can be estimated by
\[
\widehat{\mathscr{E}}_{\mathcal{A}} 
\le
C_k \Vert \mathcal{P} \Vert \, m^{-k},
\]
where $\Vert \mathcal{P} \Vert =  \Vert \mathcal{P} \Vert_{L^2(U) \to \mathbb{R}^p}$ is the operator norm of $\mathcal{P}$.

This statement is the tanh counterpart of \cite[Theorem 4.19]{LMK1}, which addresses ReLU DeepONets. We only highlight the differences in the proof. First, one should use Lemma \ref{lem:rec-fourier} instead of \cite[Lemma 3.13]{LMK1}, which then results in different network sizes in \cite[Lemma 3.14, Proposition 3.17, Corollary 3.18, Proposition 4.17]{LMK1}. Second, one needs to replace \cite[Proposition 4.18]{LMK1} with Theorem \ref{thm:holomorphic-approx}.

Moreover, in this case the trunk net ${\bm{\tau}}$ approximates the Fourier basis (\textbf{SM} \ref{app:Fourier}). From \eqref{eq:bound-fourier-basis}, one can then deduce the estimate on the $C^s$-norm of the DeepONet.
